## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION PASS** for the task-1 domain. The three extended policies, the governing base clauses, every variant parameter read, the retired dg_payment clause (written as no longer in force, not vanished, not restated with the new basis, remaining clauses in force) and the three tool contracts correspond losslessly at the level of entailment. First revision.

Policy-side notes (recorded, do not change this verdict; the policy side is not re-judged here):
- PN-1 — undeclared divergence on the lane record. Base dg_surcharges reads "the uplift of the booking's trade lane"; dg_ext_loading_surcharge (overwrite: []) reads "the uplift of the acceptance's trade lane". The KB faithfully carries both: doc_dg_approval_loading_charges_eddc9a50 "the uplift for the booking's trade lane" vs doc_dg_lane_uplift_0e41037e "Which lane is read? The lane on the acceptance record." The acceptance's trade_lane is defined at application as the booking's lane, and in both task worlds the two coincide, so no scored value is affected; a booking re-routed after application would make the two sentences disagree.
- PN-2 — parameter_schema describes contract_surcharge_discount_pct as "Discount on the base surcharge", while every rule (base and extended) applies it to the uplifted surcharge. The KB follows the rules ("it never touches the base amount on its own").
- PN-3 — the dg_ext_remittance_application overwrite retires "A remittance is applied to one acceptance," while its own rule re-asserts "A remittance the customer quotes is applied to one acceptance". The KB renders this as a retired "opening provision, which simply had a remittance applied to one acceptance" alongside the in-force "Each quoted remittance goes to a single acceptance" — faithful, but the retire-then-restate shape of the source makes the retired surface read oddly.
- PN-4 — scope of the remittance prerequisites. The policy declares that it governs covering remittances only, while its prerequisite sentences say "before a remittance is applied" / "before any remittance is applied". Whether the loading charges must also be booked before a partial remittance under base dg_payment is not settled by the source; the KB carries the prerequisites inside the covering rule's figure (doc_dg_account_charges_a909fb62) and, generally, that loading charges are "part of what the acceptance owes". Task 1 is a covering remittance and is unaffected.

## explicitness

Hop marks carried from blind_answer: H1–H5 derived. Whole-corpus read plus the n-gram and gating-keyword sweeps described in policy_kb/dangerous_goods_desk/0.md.

**KB-EXPLICIT PASS** for task 1.

- The remittance-side principle (doc_dg_account_charges_a909fb62) states a property of the figure — what a complete account includes and that an incomplete one cannot ground the applied amount — and names the kinds of charge that completeness covers, as the source rule does. It names no action, tool or order; the solver still has to establish from the ledger that both rows are missing on this file and from the two "falls due" documents that both are owed now. This is the closest sentence to the line in the task-1 domain and is recorded as an observation, not a finding.
- doc_dg_charges_due_balance_8791fa91 "The balance field on the acceptance shows a different figure from the rebuilt one. The rebuilt figure governs." restates the source's own "rather than read from the balance shown on the acceptance"; it does not mention loading charges. Not recorded.
- Titles and openings of the task-1 documents name general subjects ("Charges Counted Against a Remittance", "Applying a Remittance That Covers the Charges Due", "When the Hazardous-Cargo Surcharge Falls Due", "When a Marine-Pollutant Surcharge Is Owed"); the covering-remittance title is the declared subject of dg_ext_remittance_application, not a mirror of the caller's situation.
- No example or FAQ walks from a remittance to a surcharge booking; the invented worked cases stay inside one rule each.
- No charter sentence copied (no 11-token overlap with the yaml); no templated sentence across the task-1 documents beyond identifiers, table rows and section headings.
- Findability: the surcharge documents are reachable from the remittance principle through the record vocabulary ("hazardous-cargo surcharge", "marine-pollutant surcharge", charge codes `dg_surcharge` / `marine_pollutant_surcharge`, "loaded", "departed").
- Corpus-level defects that do not bear on task 1's hops (doc_dg_amended_declaration_review_c84489cb, EX0-1 … EX0-5) are recorded under task 0.
